summary: Diffusion language models can write several tokens in one forward pass, and they decide during generation how many passes to spend. Two outputs of the same token length can therefore vary a lot in cost.
takeaways: To understand the underlying factors of this cost variation, we analyze two diffusion models across 10 tasks.
The final answer is cheap when it repeats the model's reasoning trace and costly when it adds something new.

Taken together, our results show that diffusion's computational advantage depends on how much of the output is already determined, while its decoding effort offers a practical signal for making inference more efficient and reliable.
